basis: Congenital interruption of the inferior vena cava is a structural venous disorder.

Faciodigitogenital syndrome with defining skeletal and digital abnormalities; genital abnormalities have no axis.
Inherited retinal degeneration with rod-cone dysfunction and progressive visual loss.
Dermatan sulfate biosynthesis disorder with defining contractures and skin fragility; retinal detachment and visual abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Bruising reflects tissue fragility.
Typical features include developmental impairment, digital malformations and dental/palatal anomalies. Cardiac, renal and hearing abnormalities lack established >=30% frequency.
Familial adenomas arise in the pituitary endocrine gland; neurologic injury is not a defining or consistently common feature.
Large cell carcinoma originating in the lung, detected only through sputum cytology.
Neural tube defect with encephalocele, an occipital skull defect and severe cervicothoracic vertebral abnormalities.
Microcystoid degeneration located in the peripheral retina.
Developmental delay affects 24/28 and intellectual disability 18/28. Hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease; joint hypermobility affects only 8/28.
Global developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome; vertebral fusions and contractures are optional features without established common frequency.
Hepatic fat accumulation, inflammation and fibrosis define the disease; associated diabetes and dyslipidemia are separate conditions.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines Down syndrome; congenital heart defects affect ~40-50%, chronic hearing impairment ~50-75%, and functional ocular abnormalities >30%.
Tumor arises in vulvar reproductive glands, including Bartholin and minor vestibular glands; these have no axis.
VIM-related nonsyndromic cataract directly affects the lens.
Bone fragility and skeletal deformity define the disorder; permanent tooth agenesis affects 2/5 (40%). Motor delay reflects skeletal disease; blue sclerae do not impair vision.
Inherited retinal dystrophy caused by heterozygous SNRNP200 variants.
Congenital narrowing of the pulmonary arterial outflow above the pulmonary valve; this is a cardiovascular lesion.
Vaginal developmental malformation has no axis; associated renal malformations are separate anomalies and are not established in >=30%.
Heterogeneous nuclear-lamina disease umbrella with prominent skeletal and cardiac muscle disorders; neurologic, lipid, skin and blood manifestations are subtype-dependent.
Generalized subcutaneous fat loss and disordered lipid metabolism define CGL1; hepatic ectopic fat is common, with hepatomegaly in 8/8. Cardiomyopathy occurs in only 5-29%.
Intellectual disability affects 5/5 with frequent callosal abnormalities. Mild clinodactyly and facial dysmorphism do not establish functional skeletal damage.
Skeletal myofibril degeneration defines the group. Cardiac involvement varies by subtype and is not securely >=30% overall; respiratory muscle weakness remains musculoskeletal.
Squamous cell carcinoma arises in the oropharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis under the specified mapping.
